current_state.fact: Frontend functional verification already runs through Playwright using frontend/playwright.config.cjs with testDir=./e2e, serial execution (workers: 1), retained traces on failure, and failure screenshots.

The canonical frontend execution wrapper is ./scripts/run_e2e.sh; it validates backend health, backend API health, frontend container health, and frontend API proxy health before invoking Playwright in the dedicated Docker E2E container.
The repository already contains targeted frontend E2E specs covering smoke, create/read, billing bridges, week/today surfaces, admin screens, localization, console hygiene, and failure paths.
The existing repo-level smoke bundle named in verification-matrix.md is ./scripts/run_e2e.sh e2e/admin.smoke.spec.ts e2e/core-ux.spec.ts e2e/report-create.spec.ts e2e/quality.spec.ts.

User intent for this slice prioritizes functional reliability gates: pages must load without crashes, primary navigation and tap/click/open interactions must work, and core business flows must behave correctly; coverage growth remains secondary and ongoing.

local_adaptation.rule: For this slice, Playwright E2E is the canonical frontend functional reliability verifier.
For this slice, functional reliability gates take precedence over line-coverage expansion.
For this slice, key tests MUST assert product outcomes and semantic correctness, not merely node existence, visibility, or open-state transitions.

Fallback copy MAY be accepted only when fallback is the product-contractually correct result for the scenario under test; fallback copy MUST NOT be used as passing evidence when real data is the required product outcome.
Coverage growth SHOULD continue opportunistically, but workers MUST NOT substitute coverage metrics for broken page loads, broken interactions, or broken business-path behavior.

All execution guidance in this packet MUST preserve the project-level AGENTS protocol: frontend work requires frontend quick verification after every significant change, and crash/500 regressions require a reproduction test before fix completion.

objective.goal: Define an execution-ready frontend reliability gate focused on whether critical user and admin surfaces load cleanly, support primary interactions, and complete core business paths without functional regressions.
objective.business_value: Reduce the probability that users or operators encounter blank screens, 500s, blocked taps/clicks, broken navigation, or stalled create-to-read/report-management flows even when line coverage is still expanding incrementally.

reliability_gate.definition: A frontend slice is reliable when the scoped pages render without crash or server error, the primary user-visible interactions complete successfully, and the target business flow reaches the expected semantic outcome under Playwright verification.

required_dimensions.dimension: Route loads with no fatal render failure, no 500-visible state, and no broken proxy dependency for the tested scenario.
Primary interactions such as tap, click, open, submit, dismiss, and navigation succeed on realistic device-sized paths.
The tested flow reaches the correct business result such as report creation, read continuation, fallback rendering, admin access, or entitlement-visible state.

The asserted UI state reflects the correct product meaning: the right content, status, and data mode are shown for that scenario, including correct distinction between valid fallback and expected real data.
Critical console/runtime failures are surfaced by dedicated checks so a visually loaded page with hidden JS errors does not count as reliable.

non_goals.item: This gate does not require exhaustive route-by-route coverage parity before execution can start.
This gate does not replace broader UX refinement, visual polish, or coverage-threshold initiatives.
This gate does not require full-regression on every small change; it requires a minimally sufficient targeted profile that keeps the touched functional slice green.

surface_group.surface: /home and bottom-nav shell behaviors represented by core UX coverage
report creation workflow and resulting read/open continuation
today/week/read surfaces already covered by targeted E2E suites
ten-year/year read surfaces and week fallback/live variants where applicable
admin users, clients, entitlements, diagnostics, operations, and RBAC where already present in E2E inventory
explicit failure-path handling such as report failure states and fallback rendering

excluded_from_primary_gate.item: Pure visual-baseline expansion and screenshot breadth beyond what is needed to prove functional readiness.
Coverage-percentage targets not directly tied to crash/interaction/business-path reliability.
Non-critical exploratory specs with no direct relation to the active reliability risk.

use_case.summary: User can open the core frontend surfaces without blank screens, crash loops, or obvious broken server states.
use_case.scenario: Landing/home shell loads and exposes primary anchors/navigation affordances.
History and profile-related routes load into actionable states instead of error shells.
Admin smoke pages load for authorized operator flows without fatal render breakage.

use_case.summary: User can complete the first-order interactions that prove the screen is operational, not merely rendered.
use_case.scenario: Buttons, links, tabs, disclosures, toggles, and bottom-nav/open actions respond correctly on realistic paths.
Mobile-sized tap paths continue to work for key surfaces such as day/week disclosure and navigation-heavy screens.
Create/profile/edit flows accept user input and move to the next valid state.

use_case.summary: Critical GRACE business flows complete end-to-end through the frontend semantics that matter most.
use_case.scenario: User can start from create/storefront, submit the primary flow, and reach read/result semantics or the correct follow-up state.
Checkout/return bridge flows preserve the expected open/read continuation for supported one-off/report paths.
Operator can access core admin views and complete the key health/management interactions already represented by smoke and targeted specs.

use_case.summary: User sees controlled fallback/failure states where intended instead of uncontrolled crashes.
use_case.scenario: Week fallback/read surfaces render bounded fallback content rather than empty/error output.
Known failure-path screens surface stable error handling semantics.
Critical runtime/console issues are caught by explicit route-console or equivalent guard coverage.

business_invariants.invariant: Frontend reliability is judged first by functional behavior at user-visible surfaces, not by test count or coverage percentage.
A passing gate must prove the route both renders and supports the primary user action expected from that route.
Business-path suites remain required whenever a surface depends on backend or billing semantics; a page that loads but cannot complete the flow is not reliable.
Health checks in ./scripts/run_e2e.sh are part of the reliability contract and MUST remain in the execution path.
When a page has a known fallback contract, the reliable state is the correct bounded fallback, not necessarily the fully enriched happy-path payload.
Coverage expansion work remains welcome, but reliability gates MUST stay executable even if coverage tasks are deferred.

existing_test_assets.asset: `./scripts/run_e2e.sh` canonical Docker Playwright wrapper with backend/frontend/proxy health checks.
`frontend/playwright.config.cjs` with serial worker model, traces on failure, screenshots on failure, `testDir` set to `frontend/e2e`.
`frontend/e2e/quality.spec.ts` and `frontend/e2e/route-console.spec.ts` for quality and runtime-signal guardrails.

`frontend/e2e/today-daybrief.spec.ts`, `frontend/e2e/week-page-fallback.spec.ts`, `frontend/e2e/week-home-refresh.regression.spec.ts`, and `frontend/e2e/week-live.spec.ts` for key read/fallback/week reliability slices.

expected_failure_handling.item: If a targeted page returns a crash, blank shell, or 500, workers MUST add or update the reproduction Playwright test before declaring the fix complete.
If a route loads but a primary interaction fails, the slice remains red until the interaction path is reproduced and passes.
If a business flow depends on backend state or billing bridge behavior, workers MUST verify the exact path with the relevant targeted E2E suite rather than relying on page-load smoke alone.
If no existing spec cleanly captures the regression, workers MUST add the minimally scoped Playwright case near the closest existing bundle.
If last-failed is empty or insufficient, workers MUST run the specific impacted spec file or grep-selected test title that proves the fix.

known_defects.defect: Frontend functional reliability expectations exist across AGENTS, verification matrix, and scattered E2E suites, but they are not yet assembled into one execution packet centered on reliability-first gates.
Current smoke guidance exists, but the explicit distinction between page-load smoke and business-path reliability is not frozen in one worker-facing slice.
Recent frontend hardening work can be misread as coverage-first; this packet resolves the priority in favor of operational functional confidence.
The repo has many useful Playwright specs, but the minimal reliability bundles per route class are not yet documented as a canonical execution ladder.

success_criteria.criterion: Packet defines frontend functional reliability as a gate over load health, interaction health, business-path health, and signal hygiene.
Packet maps the existing Playwright inventory into an execution ladder from quick smoke to targeted business-path verification.
Packet gives workers a reliability-first rule set that keeps coverage growth secondary instead of substituting for functional proof.
Packet preserves AGENTS testing discipline, including frontend quick verification after significant changes and reproduction-first fixes for crashes/500s.
Packet is execution-ready: a worker can choose the touched surface, run the corresponding targeted commands, and know when the slice is green.
